questions.q: What does the KQL `render` operator actually do to the query's results?
options: It filters out rows that don't match a condition
It permanently deletes the underlying log data
It aggregates rows into a smaller summary table
Nothing to the data itself -- it's a display instruction telling the engine how to draw the already-finished table
questions.explain: render doesn't filter, aggregate, or transform data the way where or summarize do -- it's appended after the real work of shaping the data is done.

questions.q: What column shape does `render timechart` expect?
options: A single column with no grouping or binning
Only text columns, with no numeric data at all
A column of boolean true/false values only
A time-binned column plus one or more numeric columns, plotted over time
questions.explain: timechart is built for "how did this change over time," so it needs a bin(TimeGenerated, ...) column plus a numeric column to plot.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when does a piechart stop being a readable choice?
options: Only when the query includes a where clause
As soon as there is more than one row of data
Once there are more than roughly six or seven categories/slices
Piecharts are never a readable choice for KQL output
questions.explain: A piechart wants a small number of categories where share-of-the-whole is the useful framing; it stops being readable past six or seven slices.

questions.q: Inside a workbook's query step, how is the chart type usually set, compared to running a raw query in the Logs blade?
options: Through the query step's own visualization settings dropdown, rather than relying only on a trailing render line
render has no effect anywhere inside a workbook
It can only ever be a table, never a chart
By editing the Azure Workbooks source code directly
questions.explain: A workbook's query step typically uses its own visualization-settings dropdown, which offers additional layout and formatting controls beyond what render alone exposes.

questions.q: A query ends with `summarize count() by AlertSeverity`. Which render type best fits that output as written?
options: piechart only, because barchart requires a time column
barchart or piechart, since the output is a category (severity) plus one numeric column
None -- this output can never be rendered as a chart
timechart, because every KQL query is inherently time-based
questions.explain: The output is a category column (AlertSeverity) plus a count, which matches the shape barchart or piechart expect -- not the time-binned shape timechart needs.
